idiom_name: logic in its own translation unit + struct of function pointers as the outbound seam (Unity links the tests)
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the split happens at module and link level: move the decisions out of the framework callback into a function in its own translation unit that takes all inputs as arguments and returns a result, and keep the callback as a shell that gathers the values, calls that function and applies the result. Outbound collaborators are injected as a struct of function pointers, so a test links a fake instead of the driver; where the source cannot change, the GNU linker's --wrap substitutes a double at link time, though only for undefined references, so the call being replaced must come from another translation unit. Unity then drives the logic function directly (setUp/tearDown reset module state); the shell itself stays out of the unit tests because it needs the toolkit or the hardware to run.
pitfalls: Leaving the logic in a static function of the callback's own translation unit hides it from the test binary and from --wrap: the linker only redirects undefined references, so an internal call is never intercepted (the ld manual states this explicitly).
C has no fixtures: a shared static buffer or cached struct makes extracted functions order-dependent, so tests must reset module state in setUp(), which Unity calls before every test.

Routing every outbound call through a function-pointer table costs an indirection plus an explicit context pointer, and it forces the production code to carry test-oriented seams; measure before adopting it on time-critical paths.
